children: The Indian rupee opened lower against the US dollar on September 22, as a decline in crude oil prices and long-dated US Treasury yields supports risk sentiment, with importer hedging demand capping gains for the currency.
The rupee opened 6 paise higher at 95.75 per dollar, compared with Monday’s close of 95.81.

According to Finrex, the Rupee is expected to open around 95.70 this morning with Brent crude lower at $ 101.08 per barrel (it went lower than 100 also overnight) while dollar index was up to 100.39 levels.
Overall RBIs selling, good inflows in the form of Foreign capital (for IPOs and Bonds) has kept rupee above 96.00 levels and it may continue for some more time as oil remains lower.
Exporters are expected to sell the dollars at the current levels while importers may keep buying the dips for their near term requirements, it added.

Asian currencies traded mostly higher against the US dollar, with the South Korean won rising the most by 0.888%, followed by the Taiwan dollar (+0.234%) and Philippines peso (+0.198%). The Thai baht (+0.087%), Malaysian ringgit (+0.064%), Chinese renminbi (+0.036%) and Singapore dollar (+0.016%) also gained marginally. Meanwhile, the Indonesian rupiah fell 0.499%, while the Japanese yen slipped 0.013%.

The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six other units, was at 100.4, just shy of a seven-week high. Traders are pricing in a 56% chance of a hike in October, compared with 43.5% a week earlier, CME FedWatch tool showed.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens higher at 95.75 per dollar; Asian peers gain
